_meta.description: Agent-utterance -> MCP surface routing scenarios for the tool-selection advisory slice (docs/concepts/mcp-surface.mdx: the real constraint on the tool budget is model selection accuracy and description overlap, not the count).
_meta.authoring: Each utterance is phrased the way a coding or personal agent states an INTERNAL need mid-session, not as a tool invocation. Near-miss pairs are deliberate and dense: search vs get_facts vs get_memories, briefing vs handoff, revise vs resolve vs remember. An utterance never names its target tool.
_meta.toolScenarios: expected_tool is one of the 11 registered tools (apps/server/src/mcp/tools.ts TOOLS). 5 per tool.
_meta.surfaceScenarios: A SEPARATE array whose correct target is NOT a tool — the memory resource template or one of the 2 code-defined prompts. Kept distinct so the tool metrics stay clean; the slice scores these only as tool-attraction (how confidently a non-tool need is pulled onto a tool description), because prompt/resource descriptions are not in the committed registry capture.
_meta.synthetic: Every utterance is synthetic. No production content, no real identifiers.

surfaceScenarios.utterance: I hold the exact identifier and only want the stored body; address it directly so the client can cache the read instead of spending a call.
Read this memory at its stable URI, the immutable fields only, because I will read the same one again later this session.

Give me the canned orientation workflow this server ships, the one that tells me how to open a session.

Walk me through the wrap-up template the server defines for reviewing and persisting what happened.
